title: Twenty games a day

scenes.say: Your child plays twenty games a day... and the rating hasn't moved in months.
scenes.label: 20 games a day

scenes.say: Here's what nobody tells you. Almost every one of those games repeats the same mistake.
scenes.label: Same mistake

scenes.say: Fast games don't fix a habit. They put it on autopilot.
scenes.label: Autopilot

scenes.say: So more games feels like practice, but the line stays flat.
scenes.label: More games

scenes.say: A study of chess players found the best predictor of skill wasn't tournament play. It was serious study, alone.
scenes.label: What predicts skill

scenes.say: What works: one slow game, then ten minutes with a coach finding the one mistake that cost it.
scenes.label: One game. One review.

scenes.say: Your child doesn't need more games. They need better ones.
scenes.label: Better, not more

caption_hook: 20 games a day and the rating won't move? Here's why 👇
caption_body: More games usually means the same mistake, faster. One slow game with an honest review teaches more than twenty fast ones.
comment_prompt: How many games a day does your child play? Be honest.

title: The ride home

scenes.say: Your child just lost the last round. The car is silent.
scenes.label: The ride home

scenes.say: You want to help, so you ask what went wrong.
scenes.label: Wrong moment

scenes.say: But right after a loss, their head is flooded. Nothing you explain will stick.
scenes.label: Flooded

scenes.say: What does stick is the feeling: I lost, and I let them down.
scenes.label: I let them down

scenes.say: So tonight, say one thing only. I'm proud of how you fought.

params.say: I'm proud of how you fought.

scenes.label: Say this

scenes.say: Tomorrow, when everyone is calm, the game gets reviewed with the coach. One thing to fix.
scenes.label: Review tomorrow

scenes.say: Kids who feel safe after losing are the ones who keep improving.
scenes.label: Safe to lose

caption_hook: The car ride after a loss matters more than you think 🚗
caption_body: Save the analysis for tomorrow. Tonight your only job is to be on their side.
comment_prompt: What do you usually say in the car after a tough loss?

title: One second per move

scenes.say: Your child sees a move... and plays it in one second.
scenes.label: One second

scenes.say: The queen lands on a square where it can simply be taken. Game over.
scenes.label: Blunder

scenes.say: It isn't talent. And it isn't focus.
scenes.label: Not talent

scenes.say: It's a habit. See a move, play the move. Nothing in between.
scenes.label: See it. Play it.

scenes.say: Strong kids add one question before every move: what does my opponent want?
scenes.label: One question

scenes.say: It takes three seconds. And it saves more games than any opening.
scenes.label: Three seconds

scenes.say: Have them say it out loud, every game, for one week.
scenes.label: One week

scenes.say: Your child doesn't need to think faster. They need one pause.
scenes.label: One pause

caption_hook: Does your child move before you can blink? ⏱️
caption_body: Playing too fast is a habit, not a talent problem. One question before every move changes it.
comment_prompt: Does your child play too fast or too slow?

title: You're so smart

scenes.say: Your child wins a game, and you say it without thinking: you're so smart!
scenes.label: You're so smart

scenes.say: It feels like love. But here's what a child hears.
scenes.label: What they hear

scenes.say: If winning means I'm smart... then losing means I'm not.
scenes.label: And if I lose?

scenes.say: In a famous study, children praised for being smart started avoiding hard problems. Children praised for effort chose harder ones.
scenes.label: The praise study

scenes.say: In chess, that's the kid who is afraid to play stronger opponents.
scenes.label: Afraid to lose

scenes.say: So praise what they control. I loved how long you thought on that move.

params.say: I loved how long you thought.

scenes.label: Praise the thinking

scenes.say: Kids repeat what we celebrate.
scenes.label: They repeat it

caption_hook: The compliment that quietly makes kids afraid to lose 💬
caption_body: Praise the thinking and the effort, not the talent. Kids repeat what we celebrate.
comment_prompt: What's the first thing you say after your child wins?

title: The Sunday binge

scenes.say: Three hours of chess on Sunday. And nothing for the rest of the week.
scenes.label: Sunday binge

scenes.say: By hour two, your child's head is full, and very little of it sticks.
scenes.label: Full

scenes.say: Decades of learning research agree: the same practice, spread out, is remembered far longer.
scenes.label: The spacing effect

scenes.say: So split it. Fifteen minutes a day beats three hours on Sunday.
scenes.label: 15 min a day

scenes.say: A few puzzles at their level, solved slowly. No guessing.
scenes.label: Slow and honest

scenes.say: Seven small sessions. Seven chances to remember.
scenes.label: Every day

scenes.say: Your child doesn't need longer sessions. They need more of them.
scenes.label: Shorter. More often.

caption_hook: 3 hours on Sunday or 15 minutes a day? The research is clear 👇
caption_body: Same total time, very different results. Short daily practice is remembered far longer than one long session.
comment_prompt: When does your child practise: every day or weekends?

title: Six months flat

scenes.say: Same rating for six months. Your child trains, plays, tries... and nothing.
scenes.label: 6 months flat

scenes.say: And you start to wonder: is this their limit?
scenes.label: Their limit?

scenes.say: But look at their last losses. Most of them are lost in exactly the same way.
scenes.label: The same way

scenes.say: The rating is only what you see. Underneath, there are two or three habits.
scenes.label: Under the rating

scenes.say: A good coach finds the one that costs the most, and fixes that one first.
scenes.label: One at a time

scenes.say: Fix one habit, and the line that was flat starts to move.
scenes.label: Then it moves

scenes.say: A plateau isn't a limit. It's a signal.
scenes.label: It's a signal

caption_hook: Stuck at the same rating for months? Read this 👇
caption_body: A plateau usually means the same two or three habits keep repeating. Find the one that costs the most and start there.
comment_prompt: How long has your child been at the same rating?

title: Watching isn't training

scenes.say: Your child watches chess videos for hours. And it really looks like studying.
scenes.label: Looks like studying

scenes.say: But a classic study found we remember what we pull out of our own head, far more than what we just go over again.
scenes.label: The testing effect

scenes.say: Watching feels easy. Solving feels hard. And the hard one is the one that sticks.
So for every video: one position they solve alone. No hints.
scenes.label: One video, one puzzle

scenes.say: And someone who looks at their own games, not a grandmaster's.
scenes.label: Their own games

scenes.say: That's when patterns move in... and stay.
scenes.label: Patterns

scenes.say: Videos are dessert. Training is the meal.
scenes.label: Dessert vs meal

caption_hook: Is your child watching chess or training chess? 🎥
caption_body: Videos inspire, but kids improve by solving and by fixing their own mistakes. A simple rule: one video, one puzzle.
comment_prompt: How much chess does your child watch vs solve?

title: Is my child talented?

scenes.say: Every chess parent secretly asks the same thing: is my child talented?

params.question: Is my child talented at chess?

scenes.label: Talented?

scenes.say: In every club there are a few kids who learn fast at the start.
scenes.label: The fast starters

scenes.say: But among players who became masters, some got there in about three thousand hours of practice. Others needed more than twenty thousand.
scenes.label: Same title

scenes.say: So a fast start doesn't decide it. And a slow start doesn't either.
scenes.label: Not decided yet

scenes.say: What you can't see matters more: how they train, who guides them, and whether they love it.
scenes.label: What decides it

scenes.say: And those three things, you can actually do something about.
scenes.label: You control this

caption_hook: "Is my child talented at chess?" The honest answer 👇
caption_body: Talent is real, but it decides far less than parents think. How a child trains, and with whom, matters more.
comment_prompt: At what age did your child start playing chess?

title: Tournament morning

scenes.say: It's tournament morning. Your child is pale, quiet, and barely touches breakfast.
scenes.label: Tournament morning

scenes.say: You want to help, so you start giving advice. But last-minute advice only adds weight.
scenes.label: Last-minute tips

scenes.say: Step one. Arrive early. Ten calm minutes in the hall beat any last-minute lesson.
scenes.label: Step 1 Early

scenes.say: Step two. Give them one job, not ten. Before every move, ask what the opponent wants.
scenes.label: Step 2 One job

scenes.say: Step three. One sentence before they walk in: I love watching you play.
scenes.label: Step 3 One sentence

scenes.say: Kids who walk in calm think longer, and see more.
scenes.label: Calm kids see more

scenes.say: Your child doesn't need a pep talk. They need your calm.
scenes.label: Your calm first

caption_hook: Tournament morning nerves? Do these 3 things 👇
caption_body: Last-minute advice adds pressure. Arrive early, give them one job, and say one kind sentence before they walk in.
comment_prompt: What do you say to your child right before a round?

title: Giving pieces away

scenes.say: Your child is winning... and then gives a piece away for free. Again.
scenes.label: Another piece gone

scenes.say: You say: be careful. But careful isn't something a child knows how to do.
scenes.label: Be careful

scenes.say: Step one. Hands under the table until the move is chosen.
scenes.label: Step 1 Hands

scenes.say: Step two. Before every move, one check: is anything of mine attacked?
scenes.label: Step 2 One check

scenes.say: Step three. At home, a few easy puzzles a day, solved slowly, never guessed.
scenes.label: Step 3 Slow puzzles

scenes.say: After a few weeks, the free gifts get rare, and the games last longer.
scenes.label: Fewer gifts

scenes.say: Careful isn't a personality. It's a routine.
scenes.label: A routine

caption_hook: "Be careful" doesn't stop blunders. This does 👇
caption_body: Children can't act on "be careful". Give them a routine instead: hands still, one check before every move, slow puzzles at home.
comment_prompt: Does your child lose pieces when they are winning?

title: How many hours a week?

scenes.say: Parents ask us this every week: how many hours should my child train?

params.question: How many hours should my child train?

scenes.label: How many hours?

scenes.say: The honest answer: less than you think, if it happens most days.
scenes.label: Less than you think

scenes.say: A child learns while their attention is fresh. After that, they're just sitting there.
scenes.label: Fresh attention

scenes.say: And hours of fast games don't count. That's playing, not training.
scenes.label: Playing isn't training

scenes.say: Here's a simple test. After a session, ask what they learned. One clear answer means it worked.
scenes.label: One test

scenes.say: Don't count the hours. Look at what's inside them.
scenes.label: What's inside the hour

caption_hook: How many hours should a chess kid train? ⏱️
caption_body: Fewer than most parents think. Short, focused sessions most days beat one long one, and fast games are play, not training.
comment_prompt: How many hours a week does your child train?

title: A lesson with a plan

scenes.say: Your child has a chess lesson every week. But ask what they're working on, and nobody knows.
scenes.label: Working on what?

scenes.say: Most lessons are improvised. A new topic every week, and nothing connects.
scenes.label: Improvised

scenes.say: At Chess Talents Factory, we start by finding what is really holding your child back.
scenes.label: First, we look

scenes.say: Then every class has three parts: warm-up exercises, one clear idea, and practice games where that idea must appear.
scenes.label: Every class

scenes.say: Your child moves along a path of six levels, so you always know what comes next.
scenes.label: Six levels

scenes.say: And every three months you get a report: strengths, what to improve, and the next steps.
scenes.label: Every 3 months

scenes.say: Talent matters. A plan matters more.
scenes.label: A plan

caption_hook: Do you know what your child is working on in chess? 👇
caption_body: At ChessTalentsFactory every class follows a plan: we find what holds your child back, teach one idea at a time, and report progress every quarter.
comment_prompt: Do you know what your child's lessons are working on this month?

title: Why small groups

scenes.say: Your child sits in a big online class, camera off, waiting for it to end.
scenes.label: Lost in the group

scenes.say: In a big group of mixed levels, the lesson is too easy for some and too hard for others.
scenes.label: Mixed levels

scenes.say: At Chess Talents Factory, groups are small: two to six kids of the same level.
scenes.label: Small groups

scenes.say: Each group trains with an International Master who knows how to explain to a child.
scenes.label: International Masters

scenes.say: You always know where your child is on a path of six levels, and what comes next.
scenes.label: Six levels

scenes.say: Between classes, short assignments keep the idea alive until the next one.
scenes.label: Between classes

scenes.say: A small group isn't a detail. It's where your child gets seen.
scenes.label: Seen

caption_hook: Is your child lost in a big online chess class? 👇
caption_body: At ChessTalentsFactory groups have 2 to 6 kids of the same level, with an International Master, a clear path of levels and short assignments between classes.
comment_prompt: How many kids are in your child's chess class?

title: From 1100 to 1800

scenes.say: One of our students came to us with a rating of 1100.
scenes.label: Started at 1100

scenes.say: At that level we see the same pattern in many kids: lots of games, and no plan.
scenes.label: Games, no plan

scenes.say: So the training got a structure. Every class: warm-up exercises, one clear idea, practice games.
scenes.label: A structure

scenes.say: Thirteen months later: from 1100 to over 1800. Later came the National Master title.
scenes.label: 13 months

scenes.say: And it's not one story. More than 30 of our students have become national champions.
scenes.label: Not one story

scenes.say: More than 250 students have trained with us.
scenes.label: 250+ students

scenes.say: Every child is different. What repeats is the method.
scenes.label: The method repeats

scenes.say: If your child is stuck, it's rarely talent. It's usually the plan.
scenes.label: It's the plan

caption_hook: From 1100 to over 1800 in 13 months. A real student 👇
caption_body: No shortcut: a structured class, one idea at a time and a clear plan. Every child is different; what repeats is the method.
comment_prompt: What is your child's rating today, and where was it a year ago?

title: From 1100 to a world title

scenes.say: One of our students started at 1100. Nobody was talking about world titles.
scenes.label: Rating: 1100

scenes.say: Most kids at that level train a little of everything, and improve a little at nothing.
scenes.label: A bit of everything

scenes.say: With us, the work was different: one concept at a time, until it shows up in real games.
scenes.label: One concept

scenes.say: Two years later: from 1100 to over 1900.
scenes.label: 2 years

scenes.say: And then the title: Under-10 World Champion, in girls' rapid chess.
scenes.label: World Champion

scenes.say: And it's not only one child. More than 30 of our students are national champions.
scenes.label: 30+ champions

scenes.say: Every child is different, and we never promise a title. What repeats is the method.
scenes.label: No promises

scenes.say: Level by level, with a plan the parents can see.
scenes.label: Level by level

caption_hook: Started at 1100. Two years later: World Champion U10 👇
caption_body: One concept at a time, a class with structure and a plan parents can see. We never promise titles; what repeats is the method.
comment_prompt: What would you like your child to achieve in chess in two years?
